slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Sector area = (arc measure/360) times πr2. For a minor segment with central angle 0≤θ≤180 degrees, area=(θ/360)πr² minus its triangle area. A major segment has area πr² minus the complementary minor-segment area, equivalently major-sector area plus the small triangle area.

A sector is a "pizza slice"; a circular segment is the region between a chord and its arc. For a 90 degree sector of radius 6: sector area = (1/4)(36π) = 9π; the triangle has area (1/2)(6)(6) = 18; the segment has area 9π − 18, about 10.3.
